newsitem.title: USA: US corp debt slips with Treas, Stratosphere down.
newsitem.headline: US corp debt slips with Treas, Stratosphere down.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bonds outperformed an ailing U.S. Treasury market with the help of light month-end buying, while junk-rated Stratosphere Corp debt eroded, dealers said.

News that Stratosphere suspended construction on its new hotel tower due to an anticipated cash shortfall sent the gaming concern's 14.25 percent first mortgage notes down to an 81 offer near the close compared with an 84 bid in early trade, one trader said.
No bid was spotted late in the session, but the notes were said to trade at 82 bid near midday.

Elsewhere, ValuJet's 10.25 percent debt due 2001 rose more than one point to 88-1/2 bid, 89-1/2 offer after news the cut-rate airline received tentative Federal regulatory approval to resume operation.
The notes were quoted at 87-1/4 bid on Thursday.
Standard & Poor's said it may still cut the notes CCC-plus rating, along with its B-minus corporate credit rating.

High-grade corporate bonds were quoted down about one point in the long end in sympathy with the morning's quick erosion in the U.S. Treasury market, which fell after a jump to 60 from 51.2 in the Chicago Purchasing Manager's index.
The 30-year bond closed down 30/32 to yield 7.12 percent.

Many economists in a Reuters survey revised their forecasts for a stronger national purchasing managers survey for August, to be released on Tuesday. Preliminary results from the poll call for a rise in the NAPM to 52.5 in August from 50.2 in July.
Analysts said August jobs data, to be released next Friday, should command the most attention, however.
Investment grade corporate trade was said to be lackluster at best ahead of an early close and long holiday weekend. All markets will be closed for the U.S. Labor Day holiday.
While some traders declared the market essentially closed from the start, a handful of desks interviewed said buyers were capitalizing on higher yields in early action.
"There were a couple of buyers floating around doing a little month end purchasing," one high-grades trader said.
Spreads to Treasuries were firmer by one basis point across most sectors, one trader said.
NationsBank spreads were unchanged amid news the bank would buy Boatmen's Bancshares Inc in a deal valued at about $9.5 billion, bank and finance traders said.

The purchase is based on a fixed exchange rate of 0.6525 per share of Nationsbank common stock for each share of Boatmen's common, the companies said. At least 60 percent if the aggregate purchase price paid to all holders will be in Nationsbank common stock.
Nationsbank stock closed Friday down 7-1/8 points at 85-1/4.

Moody's Investors Service said it may raise Boatmen's A3 subordinated debt and A2 counterparty ratings after the news. NationsBank's debt ratings remain under review for possible upgrade, Moody's added.
Standard & Poor's said it placed NationsBank and Boatmen's ratings under review for possible upgrade.
No new issues were priced on Friday. Next week's slate has yet to firm, but light deal flow is expected in the run up to next Friday's U.S. employment report, syndicate sources said.
Issuance may feature $400 million in debt from telecom concern Nextwave Telecom Inc, one high-yield source said.
The Public Securities Association recommended a 1400 EDT/ 1800 GMT early close for the U.S. fixed-income markets on Friday in observance of the Labor Day holiday on Monday.
